ledger.claim: The artifacts describe the same trip and the measurement is clean. The trip record, the GPS trace and the fare ledger all carry trip_id TRP-02836; the trace runs from the recorded boarding at 18:46:16 to the recorded completion at 19:08:16, matching the trip record's start and end events. It is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with 100.0% coverage, no gaps, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and a 10-second sampling interval, so it does not meet any of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and is not impaired for policy purposes. The rider's initial burden of showing the artifacts describe the same trip (POL-RD-08(a)) is therefore discharged on the evidence, not on assertion.

On POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the trace, not the trip record's rounded copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 16.96 km against trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.0 km, and the clause says the trace figure governs and the rounded copy may not be cited for the threshold test. Any measurement of excess on this trip must therefore start from 16.96 km, the figure the platform's own derived block publishes.

The comparator is fixed by POL-RD-12. The vehicle type is RYDE_POOL, so the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the matched-itinerary optimal of 16.0 km stored on the trip record, and solo_optimal_distance_km of 11.5 km is carried for reference only. The rider does not press the 11.5 km figure as the comparator, because POL-RD-12 forecloses that comparison on its face; the rider's case is the trace measured against the 16.0 km matched itinerary.

On the rider's own evidence the trace exceeds the matched itinerary by 0.96 km, which is 6.0% of 16.0 km. That clears the 0.8 km absolute limb of POL-RD-01 but not its 20% limb, and POL-RD-01 requires both tests to pass. No route deviation is therefore established on this trip and the POL-RD-02 recomputation is not reached; the rider accepts that the arithmetic forecloses a distance-and-time refund and does not ask the tribunal to order one.

The driver's answer - that the co-rider pickup is part of the itinerary - is already comprehended in the 16.0 km matched-itinerary baseline that POL-RD-12 makes the comparator, so it cannot enlarge that baseline and cannot excuse distance beyond it. The statement points to no artifact of this trip; under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that cites no evidence ID carries no weight and is discarded, so it neither shifts the burden nor supplies an amended optimal.

No advisory covers this corridor. The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02836-01 is MISSING: it has weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and can carry no fact, and its absence is itself citable. The POL-RD-03 exoneration test needs an advisory naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses within a validity window overlapping the trace, so that test cannot be run for the driver on this record: no part of the measured distance is exonerated by an advisory.

This is a pooled trip: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL and the platform's matched pooled itinerary is stored as trip_record.optimal_distance_km = 16.0 km, computed at match time 'matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider'. Under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 baseline for a pooled trip is that matched-itinerary figure, not the 11.5 km solo figure the rider quotes from trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km. A claim that measures excess against the solo optimal has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone, and the ruling must name both figures so the rider can see why.

On the governing trace, EV-GPS-02836 records trace_distance_km = 16.96 km; POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.0, the governing measurement. Excess over the matched-itinerary optimal of 16.0 km is 0.96 km, or 6.00%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal_distance_km (3.2 km on this route) AND 0.8 km absolute, and both tests must pass. The percentage limb fails at 6.00% against a 20% threshold, so no deviation is established.

The entirety of the 0.96 km excess is the co-rider pickup, which is part of the platform-matched pooled itinerary — the driver's counterparty statement records it as such and the rider's own claim text describes 'picking up someone else'. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied, so that 0.96 km is not deviation at all.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence ids, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The measured excess of 0.96 km / 6.00% does not meet that threshold, so the burden never shifts to the driver and the driver is not required to point to any exculpatory artifact or clause to defeat the claim.

POL-RD-01 provides that where either establishment test fails no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, save only for a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). No such correction is available here: erp_gantries is empty, tolls_erp is 0.00 and the airport surcharge is 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge. The charged total of SGD 23.51 stands and, per POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute leaves payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 as they are.

The finding rests on a clean, unimpaired trace: EV-GPS-02836 carries 133 fixes at a 10 s sample interval with 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c). There is therefore no data failure and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation; POL-RD-08's burden is tested on an unimpaired trace and the admissibility weight of the deciding artifact is 1.0.

No repeat-deviation uplift or conduct referral applies. POL-RD-01 records no material deviation on this trip, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; and even if it were consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 173 — a ratio of 0.006, far below the 0.05 the clause requires and below its 3-flag alternative — so no pattern is established on the only fields POL-RD-06 (and POL-GEN-01) permit for that test.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you have been heard, and on this record the rider and the driver end up agreeing, and the evidence supports that agreement.

This was a pooled ride (Ryde Pool, trip TRP-02836). Under the route-deviation policy the comparator for a pooled trip is the matched-itinerary distance the platform computed at match time. The trip record stores that as trip_record.optimal_distance_km = 16.0 km (EV-TRIP-02836), and the platform's own source note describes it as a 'matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider'. The rider's usual route of 11.5 km is carried separately as trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km and is reference only: POL-RD-12 says a claim measured against the solo figure has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. I name both figures (16.0 km matched, 11.5 km solo) so the rider can see why the 11.5 km comparison cannot be the baseline.

The distance actually driven is taken from the GPS trace, not the trip record's rounded copy: POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km = 16.96 km (EV-GPS-02836) govern over trip_record.actual_distance_km = 17.0 km. The excess is therefore 16.96 - 16.0 = 0.96 km, which is 6.00% of 16.0 km. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to clear BOTH 0.8 km absolute AND 20% of the optimal distance (3.2 km here), and both tests must pass. The 0.96 km clears the absolute limb, but 6.00% is far short of 20%. No route deviation is established.

The rider's point that extra distance was driven picking up the co-rider does not change this. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary from excess altogether, and the 16.0 km matched itinerary already includes that pickup, so there is no deviation for it to enlarge.

Because no deviation is established, the POL-RD-02 fare recomputation is never reached. The only refund that survives a failed POL-RD-01 test is a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4), and there is none here: the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02836) carries no ERP gantry lines, tolls of SGD 0.00 and an airport surcharge of SGD 0.00, so there is no phantom gantry and no wrongly applied surcharge. The charged total of SGD 23.51 stands as billed.

Two further points on the driver's account. First, the trace is clean: 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and there is no data-failure escalation under POL-RD-10(3). Second, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02836-01 is missing from the bundle (weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT). No party relied on it as an exculpatory ground - the driver's answer is that the trip was pooled, not that traffic forced a detour - so POL-RD-03 was never invoked against it and its absence neither escalates the case under POL-RD-10(5) nor engages POL-RD-13.

On the driver's record: POL-RD-01 records no material deviation, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 173 completed trips in 90 days (ratio 0.006), below both the 3-flag and the 0.05 thresholds, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral arises.

The deciding measurements are carried by EV-GPS-02836 and EV-TRIP-02836, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is 0.90. The outcome is NO_ACTION: the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence, the charge of SGD 23.51 remains in place and no money moves (the monetary effect is SGD 0.00, below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold). This ruling was made without human review and either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
